where: Section 2, opening line of the five parts
problem: "Every active IoT device has five jobs, and usually five parts" is too strong. Many nodes are input only (a soil-moisture node has no relay or motor), and the chapter's own exam trap says a device needs a control unit, a communication module and a power source, with no mention of an actuator. A student may conclude every device must have an actuator.
fix: Say: an active IoT device combines a control unit, a communication module and a power source; most also add sensors and actuators. An input-only node has sensors but no actuator.

problem: The gateway is called "a device", but the chapter has just defined a device as the package that gives a thing sensing, computation, communication and action. A gateway usually does no sensing or actuation, so the two sentences pull against each other.
fix: Write: "A gateway is a device in the network sense: it collects data from many things and forwards it to the internet. It bridges short-range radios and the wide-area network, and it usually has no sensors or actuators of its own."

problem: The life estimate ignores self-discharge and cell ageing, so 6.2 years looks like a guaranteed field life. A careful reader of a real datasheet will find the number misleading.
fix: Add one line after the life formula: "This is an upper bound. Self-discharge and cell ageing cut real life, often by 10-20 percent per year of storage."

problem: "The identity may be an RFID tag on a parcel" confuses the carrier of the identity with the identity itself. A tag holds a code; the code is the identity.
fix: Write: "The identity may be a code stored in an RFID tag on a parcel, a serial number in a chip, or a network address."

problem: Saying a passive RFID tag has "no control unit" is loose. The tag chip does contain simple logic and memory for the stored code; what it lacks is a programmable control unit and its own power source.
fix: Say: "It has no programmable control unit, no sensor and no power source of its own; the reader powers it and reads its stored code."
